name: Chiltern

facts.claim: Gold-rush town about 25 km from Beechworth with a preserved 19th-century main street.
Dow's Pharmacy, a National Trust property, operated as a chemist from 1859 to 1968 and was donated intact in 1988.
Lake View House, a National Trust property overlooking Lake Anderson, was the childhood home of author Henry Handel Richardson.

ticketUrl_note: Town with no single steward; National Trust properties (Dow's Pharmacy, Lake View House) are extras inside it.
access_note: Dow's Pharmacy charges adults $10 (combined ticket with Lake View House $15) but that is an extra inside the town, not the price of the spot.

name: Lake Sambell

facts.claim: Lake and parkland in Beechworth with a roughly 2 km circuit and a bird hide.
The Lake Sambell to Lake Kerferd walk runs through eucalypt forest of Beechworth Historic Park with traces of old mining.
Walking is free; dogs are permitted on leash in the historic park.

ticketUrl_note: Local lake and parkland, no single official site found; Parks Victoria historic park page not verified.

name: Chiltern-Mount Pilot National Park

facts.claim: Park of about 21,636 ha of open eucalypt forest (red stringybark, mugga ironbark) between Beechworth and Chiltern.
Mount Pilot Lookout is a short walk from the car park to the 545 m summit, with 360-degree views toward Mount Buffalo.
The Whitebox Walking Track is an 8.5 km, 2-3 hour walk from Honeyeater Picnic Area; Woolshed Falls is a 10 minute drive north of Beechworth.

access_note: Wikipedia title is 'Chiltern-Mt Pilot National Park'. Pin 'Mount Pilot' name differs; app name uses 'Mount'.
unresolved: Page lists no entry fee and fees page did not show a site-specific charge; free entry assumed per Victorian national park rule.

name: Eldorado Dredge

facts.claim: Large steel gold dredge built 1935-36 by Thompson's Engineering for the Cocks Eldorado Gold Dredging Company.
It has 110 digging buckets and dredged 30 million cubic metres from the Eldorado Plain before being decommissioned.
It is on the Eldorado-Byawatha Road on the edge of Eldorado and holds an Engineers Australia heritage marker.

ticketUrl_note: Parks Victoria has a guide page to the dredge (per Wikipedia external link) but its URL was not found (guessed deep link 404); no verified official site.

name: Yackandandah Gorge Scenic Walk

facts.claim: Walk along a historic gorge dug as a tail race to sluice gravel and sand in the gold rush.
The trail follows a creek with cascading waterfalls and shady trees; the top of the gorge is steep.
A car park with information signs marks the start; walking from town along the creek takes about an hour.

ticketUrl_note: Local walking track with no single steward; tourism listing only.

name: Glenrowan

facts.claim: Small town where Ned Kelly and his gang made their last stand in June 1880.
Ned Kelly's Last Stand animated theatre at the Glenrowan Tourist Centre re-enacts the siege; Kate's Cottage and Kelly Museum, plus the Big Ned statue, are in town.
The Ned Kelly Discovery Hub at Lions Park tells the 1880 siege story and includes the original railway station.

ticketUrl_note: Town; attractions in it have separate operators.
access_note: Paid attractions inside town are extras; price not recorded.
